visualReview.notes: Inspected the site preview, four rotations and six detailed views. The layered cypress roof, raised veranda and center and side stairs retain the feature proportions of Shishinden. The dark Kenreimon and Sakuheimon are distinguishable from the vermilion ceremonial gates. The separate Seiryoden frontage, lower tiled cloisters and residential courtyards are visible.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Inspected all eleven shared viewer captures, including the dated placement and unload check. Dark timber, light plaster, both roofing surfaces and masonry display as intended. Original site relief was checked separately from the flat placement fixture.

mediumFiReview.notes: Inspected all twenty-seven context, comparison and detail images. The skyline and district levels keep the enclosure, gates and principal halls. The street and close levels introduce the full set of mapped subsidiary roofs and preserve the ceremonial court, stepped hall entrances, rafter details and tiled perimeter.

geographicReview.notes: The native palace boundary and 113 building, roof and wall features define a signed palace frame. Inspected the original 640 m unmasked terrain field, and the ground and understructure contact at the South Garden and the east veranda. Foundations and finished grades remain approximate.

fidelityReview.scope: The Kyoto Imperial Palace compound as seen in April 2017, including the Shishinden, Seiryoden, halls and residences, linking corridors, ceremonial courts, and the mapped gates and plaster perimeter walls inside the named palace enclosure.
fidelityReview.notes: Two exact Qualla images establish the Shishinden roof skirt, pale infill, deep eaves, raised veranda and the stair profile. Three gate photographs show the gabled dark outer gates and red tile-clad ceremonial typology. The Seiryoden photograph shows its polished timber porch and the band below the eaves. Roof measurements and the main tread count are tied to written palace sources, with other roof profiles inferred from the map and photographic context.

imageryReview.notes: The six exact Qualla photo files all match the Commons originals by Saigen Jiro. Native revisions credit the own work of the photographer and explicitly dedicate the photographs under CC0.

validation.sharedCaptureScope: Kyoto Imperial Palace in April 2017, including the compound wall and gate openings, main halls, ceremonial galleries and secondary palatial ranges.

limitations: The model depicts the April 2017 exterior. The Shishinden roof width, depth and overall height come from palace records. Floor, skirt breaks and trim profiles were estimated against the cleared photographs.
The ground retains the original source field. Individual foundations, finished court grades, the gate thresholds and step assumptions are approximate.

The perimeter follows the mapped enclosure and its gate openings. Its post spacing and roof cross-section are approximate. Smaller mapped ancillary roofs in the palace have estimated roof divisions, materials and heights.

Rooms, furnishings, delicate carvings, gardens and vegetation are outside the exterior structure model. Distant detail levels simplify minor roofs and retain the distinct halls, gates and compound outline.
